statement: A Crown seal is drawn in the heavy hand. A light-hand Crown seal is a forgery.
verify: Look at the seal's stroke on the manifest. Crown clerks press hard: two-pass ink, fat ring. A thin, nervous line means someone else held the stamp.

statement: A Guild seal is drawn in the light hand. A heavy-hand Guild seal is a forgery.
verify: Guild clerks sign quick and light - one thin pass. Fat ink on a Guild seal means somebody leaned on it who should not have.

statement: A Church seal is drawn in the heavy hand. A light-hand Church seal is a forgery.
verify: Faith cargo is sealed with ceremony: the heavy hand, pressed twice. A whisper-thin Church seal is a lie wearing a habit.

statement: Every crate on deck must wear the trade colour and stripe pattern declared on the manifest.
verify: Fish crates wave (teal), timber rings (amber), grain dots (gold), cloth crosses (magenta), ore diagonals (blue), faith chevrons (violet). No crate may wear another trade's colours.

statement: Faith cargo travels only under a Church seal. Any other authority on a faith manifest is a forgery.
verify: Cross-check the manifest: every faith crate demands the Church's own seal. A Crown or Guild stamp over relics is somebody smuggling under a borrowed name.

statement: The tally marks drawn on a crate must match the count declared on the manifest.
verify: Count the tally marks on the crate face, then read the manifest line. Numbers never lie to each other; people lie to both.

statement: A crate's weighed mass must match its declared mass on the manifest.
verify: Set the Brass Scale against a crate and read its drawn mass. Compare with the manifest. Ore is heavy, faith is light; the scale knows.

statement: The hull at the quay must match its registered class silhouette.
verify: Overlay the registry silhouette on the ship. A warship dressed as a cog is still a warship.

statement: The masts aloft must match the registered mast count.
verify: Count the masts against the registry page. Adding a mast does not add a lawful ship.

statement: The bow at the quay must match the registered bow shape.
verify: Round, clipper or square - the registry prints the lawful silhouette. Rake and curve do not lie, they only get lied about.

statement: Vessels flying the Redwater ensign are denied entry. No paper can cleanse that flag.
verify: Look at the pennant on the mast. Redwater crimson (RDW) is embargoed by decree - whatever the manifest claims.

statement: A ship must arrive inside the tide window declared on its manifest.
verify: The arrival bell rings at a known time. Read it against the manifest's declared window in the Tide Table.

statement: A tarped crate must hold what it declares. Undeclared goods under a tarp are smuggling.
verify: Order a Hold & Search (45s of shift time) to lift the tarps. Searching an honest captain costs you the Guild's goodwill.

statement: Seal ink must be true ink. Forged ink bleeds under the reagent.
verify: Wet the manifest with the Ink Reagent. True ink holds its line; forged ink blooms and bleeds red-brown.

statement: Erased-and-redrawn hull lines are forbidden. The lamp shows the ghost of the first stroke.
verify: Sweep the Lamp across the hull. Where a line was scraped and redrawn, the ghost of the old stroke lingers.
